text_1929fe8c4fdd: Outside DB Netz operation in CSV
text_5d886f48ce74: The rail network could not be loaded. Switch the layer off and on to retry.
text_592542a01569: Source: supplied M1 Streckennetz.csv · 33,425 records · 1,549 route numbers. The CSV does not specify its data date.
text_fc9ba5dcd225: Use Rail network to show or hide reference lines from your M1 CSV. Grey shows network sections not yet travelled. Orange dashed lines are marked under construction in the CSV. Grey dotted lines are outside DB Netz operation according to the CSV. Travelled sections and your GPS tracks appear blue or green according to passage counts. Displaying the reference network alone never counts as a journey.
text_0fb9b3b16771: On Android the rail network is packaged with the app and remains visible without internet. On the web the network file loads on first opening; later offline use requires it to remain in the browser cache. OpenStreetMap background tiles still require internet.
text_0d83493024ae: M1 rail network as a toggleable offline reference layer. Travelled sections remain blue; two passes in each direction turn them green.
text_4417896332fb: Travelled: fewer than two passes in each direction
text_6c30e00fbe9a: At least twice in each direction
text_7a563ef9b8ba: Travelled sections remain blue until you have travelled them at least twice in each direction. They then turn green. Each train journey counts at most once per direction for each roughly 100-metre route section. Multiple GPS fixes or reloading the same journey do not increase the count. Only unambiguous matches to the reference network count; GPS gaps and ambiguous matches earn no credit. The calculation uses your existing own recordings on the device and server. Without the reference network, GPS tracks remain blue.
